safi-cedvel:1-4.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for the interrogative of affirmation (لك) is attached to (نشرح), (عنك) is attached to (وضعنا), (الذي) is a relative in the position of accusative, a naʿt of وزرك (لك) is attached to (رفعنا).
Clause: «ألم نشرح ... » has no grammatical position; it is an opening clause.
And the clause: «وضعنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the opening clause.
And the clause: «أنقض ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذي), and the clause: «رفعنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the opening clause.

* Rhetoric:
Representative metaphor: in His saying, the Exalted «وَوَضَعْنا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ الَّذِي أَنْقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ».
Here his state ﷺ, as he staggers under what he imagines to be a burden of sin — though it is not a sin — is likened to the state of one whom a heavy load has wearied, whom toil and scorching heat have distressed, so that he walks exhausted and afflicted, almost falling from the weight of what he staggers under. "Putting down the burden" is a metonymy (kināya) for his protection ﷺ from sins and his purification from impurities. This was expressed by "putting down" by way of exaggeration in denying it, as someone says: "I have lifted from you the hardship of visiting," to one from whom no visit has occurred, by way of exaggeration in denying any visit from him.

safi-cedvel:5-6.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive (مع) is an accusative adverbial attached to the khabar of inna in both places..
Clause: «إنّ مع العسر يسرا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «إنّ مع العسر يسرا (الثانية) » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: the second (يسرا) being free of the pronoun or of (ال) makes it different from the first (يسرا), and from here came the sense of resumption.].

* Benefits:
- One hardship will never overcome two eases:
The ease is repeated to confirm the promise and magnify the hope.
Al-Ḥasan said: When this verse was revealed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Rejoice, for ease has come to you; one hardship will never overcome two eases." And Ibn Masʿūd said: "If hardship were in a hole, ease would seek it until it entered upon it and brought it out. One hardship will never overcome two eases."
The commentators said, on the meaning of his saying "One hardship will never overcome two eases": Allah the Exalted repeated the word "hardship" and mentioned it in the definite form, and repeated "ease" in the indefinite form. It is the custom of the Arabs that when they mention a definite noun and then repeat it, the second is the first, and when they mention an indefinite noun and then repeat it, the second is other than the first. Some of them said: with the hardship that the believer has in this world there is ease in the Hereafter. Perhaps the two eases come together: the ease of this world, which is what He mentioned in the first verse, and the ease of the Hereafter, which is what He mentioned in the second verse. So his saying "One hardship will never overcome two eases" means: the hardship of this world will not overcome the ease that Allah promised the believers in this world and the ease He promised them in the Hereafter; it overcomes only one of them, namely the ease of this world. As for the ease of the Hereafter, it is everlasting and never ends. Al-Qushayrī said: One day I was in the desert in a state of grief, and a line of verse was cast into my heart, and I said:
أرى الموت لمن أصب---- ... ح مغموما له أروح
(I see death, for one who rises grieving, as a rest for him.)
When night fell I heard a caller calling in the air:
ألا يا أيها المرء ... الذي الهمّ به برّح وقد أنشد بيتا لم
(O you man whom grief has afflicted, and who recited a line that...)
يزل في فكره يسنح إذا اشتد بك العسر ... ففكر في ألم نشرح فعسر بين يسرين
(...kept occurring to his mind: when hardship grows severe upon you, reflect on «ألم نشرح»: a hardship between two eases.)
إذا أبصرته فافرح
(When you see it, rejoice.)
He said: I memorized the lines and Allah relieved me.
[Translator's note: the verse lines are garbled in the source text, with lines broken and run together; they are rendered here as printed.]

safi-cedvel:7-8.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is a conjunction (الفاء) the second is the connecting particle of the jawāb al-sharṭ (الواو) is a conjunction (إلى ربّك) is attached to (ارغب), (الفاء) is the connecting particle of the jawāb of an implied condition.
Clause: «فرغت ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «انصب ... » has no grammatical position; it is the answer to a non-jussive-governing condition.
And the clause: «ارغب ... » is the jawāb of an implied condition, i.e. "if need calls you to ask for something, then turn your longing to your Lord in it."
